title: Cloud Connector on GCP: workload discovery service

prose.text: Workload discovery lets GCP workload metadata be used in Cloud Connector policy. It is a Zscaler-managed service reading the customer's projects through impersonation, with an optional Pub/Sub path for faster updates.

prose.label: Access it needs.
prose.text: {{search-api-quota}} {{roles}} {{apis}} {{impersonation}} {{pubsub-editor-required}} The Terraform package's handling of that grant is in [[cloud-connector.gcp.terraform-modules]].

checks.do: Whether the four APIs are enabled in each project, since the service does not work without them regardless of roles.
Whether the Zscaler service account holds Service Account Token Creator on the customer service account, and that account holds Compute Viewer, Cloud Asset Viewer and Browser at the intended scope.
Whether other tools calling Cloud Asset Inventory searchAllResources use a different quota project, when discovery is slow or failing.
Whether new VMs are expected within 5 minutes (polling) or near-instantly (Pub/Sub VM-start notifications), and which roles the Cloud Connector VM has for that path.

service.statement: The workload discovery service is a Zscaler-managed service that discovers workloads in a GCP account and fetches their user-defined tags and provider-generated attributes for use in security policies.

quotes: The workload discovery service is a Zscaler-managed service that discovers workloads in your Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account. The service also fetches associated metadata such as user-defined tags and attributes generated by cloud service providers. These tags and attributes are used in security policies.

attributes.statement: Supported attributes are labels, tags (network tags), networkInterfaces.network, networkInterfaces.subnetwork, serviceAccounts.email, machineType, zone and disks.sourceImage.

quotes: Zscaler supports the following attributes: - labels: The user-defined labels assigned to the virtual machine (VM) - tags: The network tags applied to the VM - networkInterfaces.network: The VPC network where the VM is running - networkInterfaces.subnetwork: The subnetwork associated with the VM

- serviceAccounts.email: The service account attached to the VM instance - machineType: The instance machine type (e.g., n1-standard-4) - zone: The GCP zone in which the VM is running - disks.sourceImage: The source image used to create the VM

search-api-quota.statement: The service uses the Cloud Asset Inventory searchAllResources API, which is rate-limited per project; other tools calling it should use a different quota (consumer) project to avoid shared rate-limit contention.

quotes: The Zscaler workload discovery service uses the Google Cloud Asset Inventory searchAllResources API, which enforces rate limits per Google Cloud project.
configure the tools to use a different quota (consumer) project than the project that the workload discovery service uses.

roles.statement: The customer service account is granted Compute Viewer, Cloud Asset Viewer and Browser at organization, folder or project level, with Browser assigned only in the service account's project.

quotes: Go to IAM at the organization, folder, or project level.
Assign the following roles: - Compute Viewer - Cloud Asset Viewer - Browser - Only assign this role in the service account project.

apis.statement: The IAM Service Account Credentials, Cloud Resource Manager, Cloud Asset and Compute Engine APIs must be enabled per project; without them the service does not function correctly regardless of roles and permissions.

quotes: enable the following Google APIs per project: - IAM Service Account Credentials - Cloud Resource Manager - Cloud Asset - Compute Engine
If you don't enable the APIs, the workload discovery service does not function correctly regardless of your roles and permissions.

impersonation.statement: The service uses service-account impersonation to get short-lived credentials instead of long-lived ones: on the customer's project service account, the Zscaler service account is granted Service Account Token Creator.

quotes: The Zscaler service uses service account impersonation to securely access your GCP resources without long-lived credentials.
To allow the workload discovery service to generate short-lived credentials and make GCP API calls, create or use a project service account with the required IAM roles:
Select your service account.
Enter the Zscaler service account email.
Assign the Service Account Token Creator role.

pubsub-editor-required.statement: Zscaler requires the roles/pubsub.editor role on the Cloud Connector service account, which the Cloud Connector VMs use to receive workload delta messages when workload metadata changes.

quotes: Zscaler requires you to add the roles/pubsub.editor role to the Cloud Connector service account. Cloud Connector VMs use this role to receive workload delta messages when workload metadata changes.

project-discovery.statement: The service enumerates the projects the granted roles authorize, using resourcemanager.projects.list, then uses Compute Engine and other APIs to retrieve VM metadata, map tags for policy and keep an inventory in the Zscaler cloud.

quotes: It uses the resourcemanager.projects.list role to identify all onboarded projects, and it enables polling and metadata retrieval across multiple projects.
- Retrieve VM and workload metadata. - Map tags for security policy enforcement. - Maintain an up-to-date inventory in the Zscaler cloud.

polling.statement: By default the service polls for changes every 5 minutes; for near-instant updates it supports Pub/Sub-based VM start notifications, enabled by adding roles/pubsub.owner and roles/pubsub.viewer to the Cloud Connector VM.

quotes: By default, the workload discovery service polls every 5 minutes for changes. For near-instant updates, the workload discovery service supports pub/sub-based VM start notifications.
You can enable the real-time VM start notification service by adding the roles/pubsub.owner and roles/pubsub.viewer roles to your Cloud Connector VM.

vm-start-flow.statement: In the VM-start path, Zscaler creates a Pub/Sub topic in its SaaS project and shares it with the customer project, the Cloud Connector VM subscribes using roles/pubsub.owner, a logging sink publishes compute.instances.start audit events to the topic, and a poll trigger starts immediate discovery.

quotes: Pub/Sub Topic Creation: Zscaler creates a pub/sub topic in the SaaS project.
Topic Sharing: The topic is shared with your project using a resource policy.
Subscription in Customer Project: The Cloud Connector VM subscribes using the roles/pubsub.owner role.
Logging Sink: The logging sink captures compute.instances.start audit log events and publishes to the shared topic.
Zscaler Poll Trigger: The poll trigger triggers immediate workload discovery.

terraform-package.statement: The Admin Console offers a Terraform deployment package with core_infra (service accounts, IAM roles, logging sinks) and centralized_grants (cross-project discovery permissions); it creates the service account and roles, grants impersonation to the Zscaler SaaS service account, sets up the VM-start logging sinks and configures the Pub/Sub subscriptions.

quotes: The Terraform deployment package is available in the Zscaler Admin Console as a downloadable ZIP file.
- core_infra: Creates service accounts, IAM roles, and logging sinks. - centralized_grants: Grants cross-project workload discovery permissions.
- Grants impersonation rights to the Zscaler SaaS service account. - Sets up logging sinks for VM start events. - Configures pub/sub subscriptions for workload change events.
